thread:
dmitri: heads-up — we've been seeing a small spike of soft 429s on dedicated-gpu pools around 11:20 UTC. looks correlated with long sequences + kv-cache misses.

eva: can you paste the admission log?

dmitri: sure, snippet below from admit-service at 11:19:57
```
admit: pool=dedicated-8g dropped=3 soft_429=9 tokens_in_batch=512 tokens_target=4096 avg_token_latency_ms=145 kv_miss_ratio=0.32
```

carla: kv_miss_ratio at 0.32 is high for that workload. are we accounting for kv-cache warming in token budget calc? the current heuristic assumes steady cache hit rate.

ben: we recently changed kernel-selector to prefer fp16 kernels for that model, which speeds decode but increases per-token variance when cache misses cause recompute. might push some requests over soft limits.

dmitri: yeah — profiling from last canary shows p95 token-latency jumps when cache misses occur mid-batch. continuous-batching forms the batch before we observe KV outcomes.

eva: proposal: decouple token_budget target from observed batch size by applying a reactive fudge factor based on recent kv_miss_ratio per-batch. e.g. adjusted_target = target * (1 + alpha * kv_miss_ratio). alpha=0.6 to start.

carla: also think we should bias queue admission to prefer shorter-prefix requests when we approach the soft limit. two knobs: admission_score penalize(est_remaining_tokens) and early-shed for very long tails.

nate: +1 for prefix bias. Another quick win: reduce the continuous-batcher hold window by 10ms when p50 latency > threshold to lower exposure to cache-miss variance.

ben: what about the 429 semantics? current soft 429 returns 429 with Retry-After. customers see a transient error. can we convert to 202/partial with fallback model for enterprise tenants?

dmitri: enterprise fallback is config-gated. but for public pools, soft 429 is the right UX. maybe change ratio: instead of absolute token cutoff, compute admission probability p = sigmoid((tokens_in_flight - adjusted_target)/scale) and probabilistically shed. smoother and less bursty.

carla: we should add a perf-regression test in CI: synthetic sequences with scripted kv-miss patterns and assert p95 token latency doesn't regress >10%. also surface admit metrics per-model in console (kv_miss_ratio, soft_429_rate).

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: admit/heuristics:experiment-2026-03-17 -> rolling 3/10 hosts

eva: i'll push a small prototype for adjusted_target + probabilistic-shed. will instrument admit logs with debug kv_miss_ratio per-request.

dmitri: thanks — once we have prototype, run it on canary and compare soft_429/avg_latency across same trace. if good, roll to dedicated and then tweak defaults for private deployments. :thumbsup:

ben: noted — will also run kernel-selector sweep to see if alternate kernels reduce variance on cache-miss paths.

nate: created infra ticket INF-5234 to add the CI synthetic scenario and console charts.

carla: perfect. follow-ups: eva to PR heuristic, ben to kernel sweep, nate to CI + observability. meet tomorrow 9am to review canary metrics. :calendar:
